global: Laying siege to {fief} is bold, {player}. Pity the council will be asked to pay for the damage before the walls even fall.
Some who lay siege mistake it for a conquest. {fief} has walls, and the council has memories of who broke them last time.
Ser {player} has discovered that banners are cheap and stone is not. The council will be pleased to tally the cost.
Setting up camp outside {fief} is a fine way to gather attention. A shame attention is all it will earn.
The council will convene on the siege of {fief} at dusk. Let it be recorded who chose to start it without a vote.
I trust {player} has considered the upkeep on siege engines. Ours are paid for by taxes, which the council debates.
Strange how eager some are to fight for a fief they have never governed. Ambition makes poor masonry, I find.
Every siege ends in a negotiation. I merely wonder whether {player} will be the one asking for terms or granting them.
whisper: {player}, lifting your siege of {fief} now would save us both an embarrassing council session. Consider it a courtesy.
You have chosen a poor moment, {player}. Half the banners at {fief} are reconsidering their loyalty as we speak.
A siege is a loud way to announce a grievance. Quieter channels exist, and I would gladly show you one.
Your men will tire long before the walls do, {player}. Withdraw, and we can discuss this like reasonable parties.
Do give my regards to whoever approved that siege. I am curious how they plan to feed the garrison at {fief}.
Gates inside {fief} have a way of opening for the right voices, {player}. Pause, and let us talk.
Every siege needs a supply road, {player}. I have already had mine closed, and I suspect yours is next.
Turn back from {fief} while there is still a face to save, {player}. The council rarely forgives a fool twice.

global: {player} has moved against {fief}. The council will want a formal account before anyone takes sides.
A siege at {fief} raises the question of who authorized it. I am sure the minutes will be thorough.
Bold move on {fief}. Let us see whether the banners hold longer than the goodwill did.
News of the siege at {fief} is spreading. Some will call it ambition, others will call it a tax problem.
No one has yet explained what {player} hopes to gain at {fief}. I am interested in the answer, not the banners.
Watching {fief} come under siege is never pleasant. I would rather see the matter settled at the table.
The garrison at {fief} is loyal, for now. Loyalty tends to shift when the supply carts stop arriving.
A siege of {fief} changes the map for everyone, not only those holding it. Plan accordingly, friends.
whisper: {player}, I see you have begun at {fief}. Before the wagons arrive, let us discuss what the council will accept.
Your siege is noted, {player}. I have no objection yet, though I reserve the right to form one by morning.
I hope you have a reason for {fief} that will survive a vote. Mere ambition rarely does, in my experience.
Should you need a neutral voice at the council regarding {fief}, I am willing to speak. For a modest consideration.
No hard feelings about {fief}, {player}. Politics is politics, and the seat will be filled by someone eventually.
The garrison at {fief} is asking questions, {player}. Answer them well, and I may stay out of this entirely.
I suppose the siege of {fief} is a statement. I would prefer we meet first and make it an agreement instead.
Keep your banners where they are for now, {player}. I will hear your side before I decide what mine should say.
